hypotheses.justification: `hn` is implied by the hypothesis `hα : α ^ n = ((q : ℕ) : AlgebraicClosure ℚ)`. Indeed, if `n = 0` then `pow_zero` gives `α ^ 0 = 1`, so `hα` yields `((q:ℕ) : AlgebraicClosure ℚ) = 1`. `AlgebraicClosure ℚ` is a field of characteristic zero (the very instance `Nat.cast_ne_zero` is already used in the proof to get `hq0`), so `Nat.cast_ne_one` (Mathlib/Algebra/CharZero/Defs.lean) applies and gives `((q:ℕ) : AlgebraicClosure ℚ) ≠ 1` because `q.2.ne_one` (q is a prime). This is a contradiction, hence `n ≠ 0`, i.e. `0 < n`. So the statement with `hn` deleted is still provable: start the proof with `have hn : 0 < n := by rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with h | h; · exfalso; subst h; exact Nat.cast_ne_one.mpr q.2.ne_one (by simpa using hα.symm); · exact h`, after which every use of `hn` in the existing proof (`Nat.mul_pos hn hd`, `hn.ne'` for `hα0` and for `[NeZero n]`) is unchanged. Note the degenerate `n = 0` case needs nothing else since the hypotheses `hζ`, `hα` are then literally inconsistent (α^0 = 1 ≠ q). In contrast, `(hd : 0 < d)` is genuinely necessary: for `d = 0` the conclusion demands `0 ∣ m`, i.e. `m = 0`, for every `m` with `φ ^ m ∈ H q F`, but any admissible `F` is finite-dimensional hence `(F.fixingSubgroup).comap (primeLocalToGlobal q)` has finite index (`levelSubgroup_finiteIndex` in Definitions/Def_ExtCitation_LocalLevelSubgroupsPD.lean), so some positive power `φ ^ m` (e.g. `m = index`) lies in that subgroup and hence in `H q F`, contradicting `0 ∣ m`. The other hypotheses are also used in the statement itself (`F₀`, `n`, `d`, `ζ`, `α`, `φ`) or cannot be dropped without changing the statement's meaning/truth (`hqn`, `hφ`).
